answer: Make each identity prove control of its own aged domain name. The registry asks for a signed token at a well-known path on the site, and it rejects any domain younger than a year or already claimed by another member. A pigment shop, a lotus-pond blog or a karst-cave tour page each carries a registrar fee, a renewal bill and months of waiting, and a domain cannot be split between accounts. So every fake costs its operator a fresh paid name that must age first, and the farm runs dry before it earns.
